difficultyReason: The named first pair scaffolds an AA proof, but the reciprocal identity requires identifying a second similar pair, matching its sides, and recognising that the two ratios with denominator AB add to one. Connecting that partition to the target reciprocals is the main non-trivial step.
derivation: XY is parallel to BC, so angle XAY = BAC and AXY = ABC; hence ABC ~ AXY by AA and AX/AB = XY/BC. Also XY is parallel to AD and BX is collinear with BA, BY with BD, so ABD ~ XBY by AA and BX/AB = XY/AD. Since X lies between A and B, AX/AB + BX/AB = 1, giving 1 = XY(1/BC + 1/AD), and division by positive XY gives the required identity. Both native short and worked answers support these steps. The source image and native coordinates preserve A-X-B, A-Y-C, D-Y-B and the three parallel segments; the BC arrow attachment needs the stated repair. Page 3 teaches AA and corresponding side ratios; practice p7-q7 and p9-q13b use parallel lines and nested triangles, so this is an in-scope extension combining taught methods with algebra.
variantMapping: Source 900abf77 is adequately represented for this complementary-proportion/reciprocal archetype: EF is parallel to AC, so EBF ~ ABC; BF/BC = EF/AC gives (a-x)/a = x/b, hence x/a + x/b = 1 and x = ab/(a+b). The source's alternative cross-product and cancellation route is valid but not compulsory and does not establish a distinct required similarity method. No variant import or rating is recommended on this basis.
